newsitem.title: FRANCE: French bond futures rise with U.S. bonds.
newsitem.headline: French bond futures rise with U.S. bonds.

text.p: French bond futures broke out of their recent range on Monday as the dollar's recent decline against the mark calmed fears of a German rate rise this week and the U.S. bond market supported European bonds.

In very low volume, because of holidays in France, the contract managed to breach key resistance at 129.78/80 at the end of the session and traders said the more favourable outlook should keep the market supported in the coming days.

"I'm not overly convinced the Bundesbank has the independence market gives it credit for. This bigger European question will keep German politicians leaning heavily on the Bundesbank," said Iain Lindsay at Credit Lyonnais.
"They're trying to buy time and just rattle the markets a bit and keep it on its toes. All credit to the Bundesbank but in terms of substance I don't thing they'll do anything," he said.

The Bundesbank was due to set its key repo rate on Tuesday and most expected it to set the rate at an unchanged three percent. Key policy meetings in the United States and France were also expected to result in unchanged rates.

The September bond future opened at 129.70 and spiked to close at 129.88, its highest level since August 5 as stops at 129.78 were triggered just before the end of the open outcry session. Traders said the next target was 130.06.

"The dollar is strengthening slightly again but compared with level of 1.89 seems to be quite weak and if we didn't have action at 1.90 (dollar/mark) it's difficult to see why we will have action at 1.81," Patrick Mange, economist at Deutsche Bank in Paris said.
French interest rate futures climbed with the back months the best performers.

Some traders said talk that the Bundesbank could move to a variable rate repo this week, or raise the repo rate to a new fixed level, to catch the market by surprise had knocked prices to the lows for the day.
"Some were saying they will hike by 25 basis points to clear the air, set the scene to make people understand tide has turned and then go variable from there but I think that's rubbish," said one.

The French Treasury was due to announce the size of this week's regular auction of Treasury notes or BTANs on Tuesday morning.It will be selling the two- and five-year benchmarks in French francs and would announce whether any short dated Ecu notes would be on offer.
